description: Scammer-side tactics, techniques and procedures observable in the messages of a fraud conversation, across a six-phase scam kill chain. Generated from the ScamBuster TTP taxonomy; see https://github.com/laugiov/scambuster.

predicates.description: A behaviour from the closed ScamBuster TTP taxonomy, observed in a scammer message.

entry.description: Presents an unsolicited windfall or business opportunity (inheritance, lottery, contract, compensation) as the reason for contact.
Claims to represent a government body, bank, court, police or international organization to command compliance.
Poses as a known company or consumer service (courier, marketplace, vendor) to exploit its established trust.
Sends a link or attachment the target must open to proceed (portal, form, document, tracking page).
Volunteers official-looking documents (certificates, IDs, receipts, contracts) to prove authenticity.
Builds an emotional or personal bond (affection, flattery, shared life details) unrelated to the transaction itself.
Invokes God, faith or moral duty to frame the exchange as righteous and the target as chosen.
Cites invented third parties who already benefited from or vouched for the scheme.
Instructs the target to keep the transaction confidential from family, banks or authorities.
Introduces an additional persona (lawyer, banker, diplomat, agent) who must now be dealt with.
Explains away inconsistencies, delays or contradictions the target has noticed.
Requires an upfront payment to unlock a larger promised value (transfer charge, tax, insurance).
Provides concrete payment coordinates the target must pay to (bank account, crypto wallet, money-transfer recipient).
Requests the target's personal, financial or authentication data (identity documents, bank details, credentials, verification codes, address, phone).
Claims an overpayment or presents fake payment proof, then asks part of the money back.
Changes the demanded payment rail mid-conversation (bank → crypto → gift cards → cash agent).
Imposes a hard deadline or countdown to force immediate action.
Adds new, previously unmentioned fees after an earlier payment or agreement.
Invents official procedures, codes or certificates that block progress until resolved (the narrative around the fee).

entry.expanded: Threat of loss or legal action
entry.description: Threatens forfeiture, arrest, account closure or legal consequences for non-compliance.
Leverages pity, guilt or personal hardship to compel action.
Refuses, evades or disqualifies the target's verification requests (contract, company registry, statement of work).
Asks to continue the exchange on another channel (WhatsApp, Telegram, phone, personal email).
Restricts communication to a single designated contact, address or channel and forbids others.
Issues a last demand with the threatened termination of the deal or relationship.
Returns after silence, refusal or a stalled exchange with a new angle, discount or persona.
Shows fabricated profits, balances or returns as proof the scheme works, to induce further payment.
